page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.large is an entry-tier virtual server from the High Clock Speed family running on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical Intel Xeon 6149 core running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, featuring 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 22 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance includes 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and does not bundle local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Across benchmark evaluations, the single physical core configuration yields limited computational output. The system recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 1076.0 and a multi-core score of 1279.0, reflecting bottom-quartile and bottom-decile comparative rankings respectively. Stress-ng returned 1346.89 for single-core and 1789.49 for multi-core performance. Memory throughput reached 100.02 GB/sec on cached 16 KB read operations, falling to 9.96 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 9.61 GB/sec for uncached writes. Database handling showed 609.36 operations on PassMark and 1.78 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, while static web serving throughput reached 1.49 GB/sec.

Given its reliance on network-attached storage and lower aggregate multi-core metrics, ecs.hfg5.large serves as a low-cost, dedicated-compute option for steady single-threaded tasks, microservices, lightweight web servers, and development or staging environments that require a fixed 3.1 GHz clock rather than burstable allocations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.large is an entry-tier compute instance from the High Clock Speed family, powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 6149 processor on an x86_64 architecture. Delivered via KVM virtualization, it provides 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core with 2 threads, paired with 8.0 GB of memory and a 1 Gbps network bandwidth baseline. The server contains no local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote storage volumes. Benchmark metrics reflect modest entry-level output, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 1076.0, a multi-core score of 1279.0, and 1.78 million Redis SET operations per second. While throughput across uncached memory and multi-core calculations remains in lower performance tiers, the dedicated vCPU allocation provides predictable clock speeds. This configuration is suitable for lightweight background workers, small-scale web servers, microservices, and development environments requiring stable baseline resources.
